nodes.name: Hydrothermal Titania Nanotubes Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2 g of anatase powder was dissolved in 70 mL of 10 M NaOH solution. The mixture was stirred for 1 h at room temperature and then transferred to a 100 mL Teflon bottle. This bottle was sealed in a stainless steel autoclave and held at 130°C for 24 h. After cooling down to the room temperature, the as-obtained products were filtered and washed initially with deionized water and then washed with 2 L of 0.2 M HCl aqueous solution followed by deionized water until the pH reached a neutral value. The resulting products were dried at 80°C for 18 h and then grinded in a mortar. Finally, the powders were calcined at 400°C for 4 h (ramping rate: 2°C/min).

nodes.name: Deposition-Precipitation Au/Ti-75
nodes.procedure: 0.5 g of TNT was dispersed in 25 mL of ultrapure water (18.2 MΩ) and stirred at room temperature for 10 min followed by adding ammonium carbonate (1.2 g). Then, an aqueous solution of HAuCl4·3H2O (0.0125 M, 2 mL diluted by 10.5 mL ultrapure water) was added dropwise at room temperature under continuous stirring. After stirring at room temperature for 20 min, the solution was aged for 1 h. The solid was then filtered, washed with ultrapure water (70°C, 1 L), dried at 75°C for 3 h, and finally pretreated at 75°C in air.

The results of long-time CO oxidation at a constant temperature of 30°C are shown in Figure 4a. The CO oxidation reactivity of Au/Ti-300 was higher than that of Au/Ti-75 (99% vs 63% at 1.5h). Compared with Au/Ti-300 catalyst, the activity of Au/Ti-75 increased gradually during reaction and reached a steady-state situation of about 51% after 4h.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES determined Au concentrations in fresh Au/Ti-x catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma atom emission spectroscopy analysis, which was used to determine gold concentrations in the fresh gold-titanium samples, was carried out on an IRIS Intrepid II XSP instrument (Thermo Electron Corp.).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fresh Au/Ti-75 shows no obvious Au particles (ultrasmall Au species); fresh Au/Ti-300 shows Au nanoparticles averaging 5.6±1.4 nm; used Au/Ti-75 shows Au nanoparticles averaging 9.9±3.7 nm; used Au/Ti-300 Au nanoparticles average 6.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Au/Ti-75 catalyst, no obvious Au particles were seen through the TEM image (Figure 1a,b). ... Au species of the Au/Ti-300 aggregated as nanoparticles with the average diameter of 5.6±1.4 nm (Figures 1c,d and S1b) after pretreatment.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows homogeneous Au and Ti distribution for both catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding elemental mapping was used to measure element distribution of samples under the scanning TEM (STEM) mode

nodes.characterization_summary: Au/Ti-75 BET surface area 156.9 m²/g; Au/Ti-300 BET surface area 124.5 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nitrogen adsorption-desorption (Figure S3) isotherms showed that Au/Ti-75 and Au/Ti-300 had specific surface area of 156.9 and 124.5 m²/g, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fresh Au/Ti-300: metallic Au (Au 4f_{3/2} 83.2 eV); fresh Au/Ti-75: Au^+ (83.7 eV), Au^{3+} (85.8 eV); used catalysts: both metallic Au.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a confirmed the metallic nature of gold in Au/Ti-300 with the Au4f_{3/2} peak centered at 83.2 eV and positively charged gold in Au/Ti-75 with the orbital binding energy between 83.7 and 85.8 eV which were indexed to Au^+ and Au^{3+}, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ and in situ XRD show pure tetragonal anatase TiO2 phase for both catalysts with no Au diffraction signals; TiO2 lattice stable during reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns (Figure 3b) exhibited diffraction peaks of tetragonal anatase, and no signal of Au could be detected for both gold catalysts, indicating the low crystallinity nature of both gold catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images of spent catalysts confirm Au nanoparticle morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM was also utilized to characterize the morphology of the used catalysts, which was obtained after the steady-state test. ... Figure 5. TEM images (a,c) and HRTEM images (b,d) of spent Au/Ti-x catalysts
